title: Vertex Cover by treewidth
task: Does G have a set of at most k vertices that includes an endpoint of every edge?
encoding: A finite, simple, undirected, unweighted graph G and a nonnegative integer k. The graph and budget are encoded explicitly in binary.
parameter: The intrinsic treewidth t of G.

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm decides Vertex Cover within the stated running time.

sourceBasis.step: The Vertex Cover instances produced from sparse 3-SAT have linear graph order, and treewidth is bounded by that order. A solver with the stated dependence on treewidth would solve sparse 3-SAT in subexponential time.

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides Vertex Cover within the stated running time.

sourceBasis.step: Logarithmic-treewidth Vertex Cover is XALP-hard, so it is W[1]-hard. Discard the supplied decomposition from the reduction output. For a Clique input of order n and parameter k, the output treewidth is at most g(k)(1+log₂ n) for a computable g. Use the computable cutoff for a slope at most 1/g(k). Above the cutoff the exponential factor is polynomial in n, and below it the computable exponent has a finite maximum controlled by k. The polynomial-size reduction output then gives an FPT algorithm for Clique.
